PHASE-2.md was written on 18 October, before Gate 1. This file lists every place found where it and what Phase 1 built differ, and what happens about each (PHASE-2.md 0.6). **Mechanical** differences (a name, a path, an id form) follow Phase 1 or the measured fact, and are noted here. **Behavioural** ones (they would change behaviour, a contract or a guardrail) are questions for the tech lead or the data steward; the milestone named in the row waits for the answer, M2.0 does not. Items that depend on an open Phase 1 pull request are marked **pending #n**.

Line numbers refer to `docs/build/PHASE-2.md`. Code paths under `ingest/src/neonradar_ingest/sources/` are shortened to `sources/`.

Class: **D** decided, **M** mechanical (noted, no question), **Q** question for the person named, **P** pending an open pull request.

### 2.2 Record ids (PHASE-2.md 4.4)

PHASE-2.md 4.4 says a form a Phase 1 spike already chose stays, and `contracts/C1-record.md` is the authority for ids (OD-17): loaders build ids with `make_id(prefix, kind, native)`, which gives `<prefix>-<kind>-<native>`, or `<prefix>-<kind>-<first 20 hex of SHA-1(native)>`. A native id of parts joined with `|` always takes the hash branch, so every hashed id of 4.4 equals `make_id` over its joined parts.

| # | PHASE-2.md says | Phase 1 has | Class | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | GLEIF entity `gleif-<LEI>` (631, M2.4 at 3326) | `gleif-lei-<LEI>` (`sources/gleif/mapping.py`, `entity_id`) | M | Follow Phase 1; M2.4 reuses `entity_id()` |
| B2 | ICIJ node `icij-<node_id>`, called the Phase 1 form (634) | `icij-node-<node_id>` (`sources/icij/mapping.py`, `node_id`) | M | Follow Phase 1; M2.5 reuses `node_id()` |
| B3 | OpenSanctions entity `os-<id>`, called the Phase 1 form (643) | `os-ent-<id>` for every schema (`sources/opensanctions/mapping.py`, `record_id`) | M | Follow Phase 1; M2.7 reuses `record_id()` |
| B4 | Address ids hash `address_key` (625, 633); directorship ids hash officer id, company number, role, `appointed_on` (630); GLEIF relationship ids hash child, parent, relationship type (632) | Spike forms differ: Companies House addresses hash the full text; GLEIF addresses are `gleif-addr-<LEI>-legal` and `-hq`; directorships hash company number, appointment id and role; GLEIF ownership hashes child, parent and `direct` or `ultimate` | M | Follow the spec in the production loaders (M2.3a, M2.3c, M2.4). Spike output is never loaded into a graph, so nothing migrates; the address key is what removes duplicate addresses |
| B5 | ICIJ relationship id hashes start, end, `rel_type`, `link` (635, M2.5) | The spike hashes all eight relationship columns, including status, dates and source, and skips exact duplicates | Q tech lead (M2.5) | With the four-part key, rows that differ only in dates or status (a resignation and a re-appointment; the spike measured many `resigned` and `appointed` rows) get one id and fail C1 R4 as duplicates. Recommendation: keep the eight-column key |
| B6 | Sanctions and Parliament ids `uksl-g<group id>`, `uksl-<unique id>`, `ofac-<uid>`, `unsc-<ref>`, `eufsf-<logicalId>`, `ukparl-<member id>` (636 to 642) | `C1-record.md` says every loader id comes from `make_id`, which always has a kind segment. These forms pass R1 but have no kind. (`uksl-un-<ref>`, the `ukparl-pos-` and `-occupancy-` ids, the hashed relationship ids and `common.sanction_id` already fit) | Q tech lead (M2.1a, M2.6a) | Either add kinds (for example `uksl-grp-`, `ofac-party-`), which also changes the verbatim tests of M2.6 and M2.10a that use these forms, or record in C1 1.1.0 that list loaders may use these forms. Nothing is built yet, so nothing migrates |
| B7 | Company numbers normalised as in 7.1.2 (D1), prefix checked (624) | The spikes pad only all-digit numbers and keep prefixed ones as given | M | M2.3 and M2.4 use `neonradar_keys.ids` (M2.8) |

### 2.6 Matching keys after the M2.8 review (2.7: the spec seems wrong)

The review of M2.8 (#49) found places where the verbatim code of M2.8 does not do what the spec says it does, or does something unsafe for matching. The follow-up changes them, bumps `RULES_VERSION` to `"2"` (M2.8: "every output change needs a test and a `RULES_VERSION` bump") and adds a failing test first for each (`keys/tests/test_keys_fixes.py`). Every assertion of the spec's own `test_keys.py` still passes; none was changed on purpose. The graph mentor and the tech lead confirm the D rows in the review of the follow-up pull request.

| # | PHASE-2.md says | Found | Class | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | `assert person_key("إحمد خليل").symbols  # the Arabic index catches spellings the tagger misses` (5585) | The tagger alone gives خليل name groups, so the assertion passes with an empty index: nothing tested that the index is used | M | `assert person_key("إحمد").symbols` added to that test (only the index gives this spelling a group), and a test that it is empty when the index is disabled. No output change |
| F2 | `address_key` is None "when it has neither a postcode nor a street line" (4146, the docstring at 4753) | `len(out) >= 3` (4789) counts any three words as a street line, so "Dubai, United Arab Emirates", "Road Town, Tortola, British Virgin Islands", "Panama City, Panama", "New York, NY, USA" and "Isle of Man" got `NOPC\|` keys, which rule D6 would merge across unrelated records | D (orchestrator under OD-10; graph mentor and tech lead confirm) | A street line is a token that starts with a digit, or, in a text of at least three tokens (the spec's floor stays, so the rule never gives a key where the spec gave None), a thoroughfare or building word after a name in its segment ("EXAMPLE HOUSE"; "ROAD TOWN" is a place) or a unit word before a one-letter unit ("FLAT A"; "FLAT ROCK" is a place). The five texts, "Flat Rock, Michigan, USA" and "Office of the Registrar, Dubai" give None |
| F3 | ST is STREET at the end of a segment or before the post town, else SAINT (4785) | In "12 Example St, St Example, QQ1 2AB" the second ST starts its segment but is the second-to-last token, so the key read `12 EXAMPLE STREET STREET EXAMPLE` | M | ST that starts a segment is SAINT (`12 EXAMPLE STREET SAINT EXAMPLE`) |
| F4 | D1 normalisation: digits padded to 8 (5008, 7.1.2) | `\d` also matches Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits, which came back as non-ASCII "company numbers"; `"0"`, `"00000000"` and `"SC000000"` were accepted, so a placeholder would link unrelated records under D1 and keep records apart under X3 | M (digits); D (all zeros, orchestrator under OD-10) | `[0-9]` instead of `\d`, numbers of only zeros give None, and `has_ch_prefix` needs ASCII digits. Trade-off: a number written in other digits is rejected, not converted, so X3 cannot keep two such records apart either (rare; converting would be a further change) |
| F5 | `find_uk_postcode` returns the text without the postcode (4663) | Match positions in `text.upper()` were used to cut `text`; "ß" and ligatures such as "ﬁ" grow when upper-cased, so the cut shifted | M | Upper case letter by letter, keeping letters whose upper case is longer, so the positions index the original text |
| F6 | Name symbols from rigour (4585) | The tagger was given the raw name: a decomposed (NFD) name got other groups and a fullwidth one none | M | `_rigour_symbols(nfkc(name))` |
| F7 | `country_code` returns a "lower-case ISO alpha-2 code" (4979) | It returns FtM country codes, including `xk`, `suhh`, `yucs` and `cshh` | M | Docstring and `docs/er/keys.md` corrected; no output change |
| F8 | Notices for the two data files (M2.8 deliverable 6) | The wheel carried the MIT-derived index and the OGL-derived table without their licence texts | M | `data/ar_symbols.LICENSE.txt` (rigour's MIT text) and `data/nationalities.LICENSE.txt` (attribution and the OGL v3.0 text) are package data; a test builds the wheel offline and checks all four files |
| F9 | Limits not stated | `ch_same_as_key`: a paragraph 4 word at the very end stays a word, and anyascii folds £, € and ¥ before the equivalences; empty keys exist (`org_key("Ltd")`, `person_key(".")`, `ch_same_as_key("")`, postcode-only address keys) | M (documentation) | Stated in `docs/er/keys.md`, with a note for M2.10a that empty keys are dropped or written as NULL before they reach Splink; three further cases (Urdu and Persian heh forms, the Cyrillic letter Ѕ, `split_ch_name` on Arabic) are listed there as failing tests for the graph mentor, with no code change |
| F10 | The oracle test inputs (5521 to 5764) | #49 replaced only a denylisted person name and the retired "falcon ridge" words; generic names such as "SMITH, John Michael" and "Łukasz Wiśniewski" and company names such as "BACK TO BASICS LIMITED" stay as the spec gives them | Q data steward (Gate 2 list) | Do the OD-12 Companies House checks apply to strings that are only normaliser test inputs? No change until decided |
| F11 | D6 merges `Address` records with the same non-empty `address_key` that contains a full postcode or a street line (8137) | A text that is only a postcode gives the key `N1 7GU\|` (a postcode and no tokens), so D6 would merge every postcode-only address of one postcode across datasets | Q graph mentor and tech lead (M2.10a) | Should D6 skip keys with no tokens after the postcode? `docs/er/keys.md` asks M2.10a to keep them out of Splink; no change to `address_key` or D6 until decided |

### 2.7 The entity resolution benchmark (M2.9, #71)

The reviews of #71 found two places where the benchmark as specified would leak the right answer or put realistic names next to list and leak entities. The orchestrator decided both under OD-10; a third is a question.

| # | PHASE-2.md says | Found | Class | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Record ids `syn-erb-<p\|o>-<entity number>-<record number>` (M2.9 deliverable 3) | Every record id carries its true entity, so a resolver that read ids would score perfectly | M (2.7) | Opaque ids `syn-erb-r-<first 16 hex of sha1(seed\|entity id\|k)>`; the mapping is only in `labels/er_truth.csv`; relationship and `Sanction` ids keep the PHASE-1.md 4.4 edge form |
| H2 | Invented surnames for people with a list or leak record (deliverable 2) | Officers and PSCs of list and leak organisations kept Faker surnames, and one of them carried a real person's full name (G1) | G1, decided under OD-10 | Invented surnames also for every officer or PSC of an organisation that has a list or leak record or whose near twin has one, and for the near twins of all of these people; always three syllables; screened against the Faker, curated and `variants.NOT_INVENTED` surnames, typos included |
| H3 | Not covered | Second-degree links stay outside H2: (a) registry-only people who share an organisation with an exposed person; (b) organisations that are corporate officers or PSCs of a list or leak organisation; (c) registry-only people who are officers or PSCs of those organisations. On the small fixture the data-guardian delta review of #71 counted 207, 91 and 103 (head 9df6d16). At the head that adds the near-twin rule of H2, counting people linked through any officer or PSC record and including the twins of list and leak organisations in (b), they are 200, 83 and 78 | Q data steward | Should invented surnames also reach second-degree links? Until decided they keep Faker surnames, and the denylist and the OD-12 check cover them |

### 2.8 The resolver core after the M2.10a review (2.7: the spec seems wrong)

The data-guardian review of M2.10a (#77) ran the verbatim `cluster.py` on synthetic members and found that the order of 7.1.6 weakens two guarantees the spec states. `cluster.py`, `feature_schema.py` and `test_cluster.py` stay verbatim; the deciders of ADR-0015 choose at its acceptance.

| # | PHASE-2.md says | Found | Class | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | A `same` decision whose merge would cross P1 or P2 applies only with two reviewers or a senior reviewer (7.1.2 D7, 7.1.6) | 7.1.6 applies human decisions before D1 to D6 and judges the crossing then. A one-reviewer decision between two unflagged records V and U applies; a later D5 link from U to a listed record W brings W's flag to V. With a second, confirmed decision about U and W, the result depended on which of V's and U's ids sorts first. A decision can also make a later link break X5, X6, X8 or the cap, so a third record joins by D5 (no name check) before a flag arrives | D (orchestrator under OD-10, the stricter option) | Interim guard in `run.py` (`guard_decisions`): cluster once without the one-reviewer decisions, hold back each one whose two records then sit in clusters with different flag topics or leak status, and hold back again any whose cluster, once applied, holds a record with other flag topics or leak status than it had without them (all of them when such a record is outside every decision's cluster), until nothing changes; count them in `decisions_awaiting_second_review` (`links_by_rule.D7` counts the decisions passed to the clustering, `decisions_applied` those it applied). A one-reviewer `different` decision is outside the guard (the spec lets one reviewer keep records apart) and can also move a flag to a third record: by keeping B from a listed L2 it lets R join B by D5 before a listed Z joins B (`test_one_reviewer_different_decision_can_move_a_flag_today` pins it). For the deciders at ADR-0015's acceptance: keep the guard, or change 7.1.6 into two passes that judge D7 after D1 to D6; and whether `different` decisions need the guard too |
| G2 | "No flag reaches a person or company through a similar name" (the reading of G8 and 7.1.4 in the first ADR-0015 draft) | The strict name check compares the two linked records. With D1's hub, a registry record with a similar name that joined the company record first stays in the cluster when a list entry with the exact name joins; if the list entry's link comes first, the registry record stays a possible match. Ids decide the order: UK, OFAC, UN and ICIJ entries sort after `gbch-`, EU entries before | Q deciders of ADR-0015 | Pinned by `test_strict_name_check_outcome_depends_on_id_order`; ADR-0015 states it as a property and names two rules that remove the pinned case (crossing links first, re-judged after every merge, or a strict check against every record of the cluster being joined; with either, the pinned registry record never ends up with the list entry's flag, whatever the ids; without re-judging, a link that starts to cross after a merge would still be taken late), both changes to `cluster.py`. Neither makes the clustering independent of order: a company record linked to two list entries with the same flag, one with the exact name and one with a similar name, takes in the second only if the first one's link comes first |
| G3 | D6 links records with the same address key | Linking every pair gives n(n - 1)/2 links for a key shared by n records | M | Each record links to the smallest id of its key (synthetic and real apart); beyond the X7 cap of 30 the rest are refused. F11 (postcode-only keys) stays open |
| G4 | `test_cluster.py` is verbatim (M2.10a deliverable 10) | Its record ids have real formats: `ofac-5`, `icij-1`, `uksl-11111`, `gbch-co-00000001`, LEIs starting `549300`. M2.10a's own tests use ids and numbers chosen to look like tests (`ofac-test-1`, `99999901`, `SC999901`, a `SYN0` LEI), except where the spec's normalisation tests need a real form: the rejected `HE` form (`HE999901`) and the D1 padding example of deliverable 10 (`"1800000"` to `"01800000"`), which is replaced by a synthetic padding test (`"sy 9901"` to `"SY009901"`), because padding a digit-only number always lands in the allocated range | Q data steward (Gate 2 list, like F10) | Do the real-data rules for test ids apply to the spec's verbatim oracle tests and to its normalisation examples? No change to `test_cluster.py` until decided; it stays byte-identical to the spec |

### 2.9 The resolution-aware loader (M2.11)

The loader of M2.11 answers questions E2 and E4 and meets eight more places where the milestone's text and what Phase 1 built or the contract says differ. The orchestrator decided the behavioural ones under OD-10, taking the stricter option; the tech lead confirms them in the review of the pull request. Every query file the spec gives verbatim is byte-identical except the three named here.

| # | PHASE-2.md says | Found | Class | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | E4: `upsert_relationships.cypher` `MATCH`es both ends and returns `count(r)`; `upsert_relationships_resolving.cypher` checks no label (M2.11 deliverable 6) | Phase 1's loader checks each end's C2 label, moves a relationship whose end or type changed, and reports dangling rows. With the verbatim `MERGE`, a reload whose end moved fails on the relationship's uniqueness constraint, and the resolving query would write a `DIRECTOR_OF` to a `:Person` | D (orchestrator under OD-10, the stricter option) | Both files keep Phase 1's three protections, as E4 recommended: a relationship with the row's id between other nodes is deleted first, a type change is moved by `queries/delete_relationships.cypher`, and every row not written comes back so the report lists it as dangling. The direct query takes only rows whose ends are records of the load, whose C2 labels the mapping checked; the resolving query checks the labels in the database (`$labels`, from the C2 table) and also returns self-loops and the ends found through a `:SourceRecord` |
| J2 | E2: I11 compares `:PEP` and `:RCA` with the exact topics | C2's flag table (merged in 1.0.0) also sets `:PEP` and `:RCA` for `role.pep.*` and `role.rca.*` | D (OD-17: the contract wins; OD-10) | `queries/verify_resolution.cypher` I11 follows the C2 flag table; `:Sanctioned` stays exact |
| J3 | The derived ids of `HAS_ADDRESS` and `SUBJECT_OF` are built from the canonical ids after re-pointing, and rows that then share a type and an id become one (deliverable 3) | C2 (1.0.0 on `main`, and 1.1.0) builds them from record ids and says relationship ids "do not change after entity resolution" | D (OD-17; OD-10) | The ids keep C2's record-built form; rows of those two types that land on the same two nodes become one row that keeps the smallest id, with the first role of the spec's order and the union of datasets, counted as `duplicate_relationships_merged`. Question for the tech lead: keep this, or change C2 to canonical-built ids |
| J4 | I2: a node has `:Synthetic` if and only if `synthetic = true` | A `:SourceRecord` has `synthetic`, but C2's flag table puts `:Synthetic` only on `:Entity` and `:Sanction`, and the verbatim `upsert_source_records.cypher` sets no label | M | I2 (`queries/verify_base.cypher` and the Phase 1 test string) checks `:Entity`, `:Sanction` and every node that carries `:Synthetic` |
| J5 | The overlay test loads a `BankAccount` and an `Ownership` whose owner is a merged record id (deliverable 7, G2-14) | C1 R8 ("always") drops an account whose holder is not in the load, and strict R4 refuses a reference outside the load, so the account could never load | D (orchestrator under OD-10) | A non-strict load keeps such an account only when the graph holds its holder as a `:LegalEntity`, by id or through a `:SourceRecord` (`queries/find_holders.cypher`, read before writing); otherwise R8 drops it as before, so I4 holds. Strict loads are unchanged |
| J6 | Importing `neonradar_graph.loader` imports neither PyArrow, DuckDB nor Splink (deliverable 7) | The neo4j 6 driver imports PyArrow and NumPy itself when they are installed (`neo4j/_optional_deps.py`), and the workspace has them for the resolver | M | `test_instances.py` blocks the three in a subprocess, as an image without them would, imports every graph module, and also checks DuckDB and Splink without the block |
| J7 | L17: the loader refuses a load that mixes synthetic and real records | Phase 1's detection test case F (`detect/tests/test_circular_flow_neo4j.py`) loaded a real-looking holder with synthetic payments into the default instance | M | The test loads the synthetic fixture, then writes the look-alike holder and moves the holding itself; `test_loader.py`'s reload test uses a synthetic `role.pep` person instead of a Companies House look-alike |
| J8 | `decided_at` is the run's start time, which its id encodes | `run.json` has no start time; the run id is the folder name | M | `decided_at` comes from the run id; a `run.json` whose `run_id` is not the folder name in the `er-<yyyymmddThhmmss>-<4 hex>` form stops the load |
| J9 | Not specified: which records a load with a run must hold | A run of other records would leave stale or partial merged nodes | D (orchestrator under OD-10) | A load that replaces (L9) must hold exactly the run's resolvable records; any load refuses a merged entity with only some of its members (exit 1, counts only) |
| J10 | Branch `p2/m2-11-resolved-loader`; uv 0.11.32 accepts the test-only cycle | The orchestrator named the branch `p2/m2-11-graph-loader`; the workspace pins uv 0.13 | M | Both followed; uv 0.13.4 accepts `graph`'s `dev` group listing `neonradar-resolve` |

## 3. Cypher that Phase 1 runs from Python strings

From now on every Cypher statement that new or changed code runs lives in a `.cypher` file, so `make cypher-lint` checks it (M2.0 item 11). These move into files when a later milestone touches the code, not in M2.0.

| Where | Statements | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `graph/src/neonradar_graph/smoke.py` | `COMPONENTS`, `APOC_VERSION`, `GDS_VERSION` | Neo4j, APOC and GDS versions (`api/src/neonradar_api/health.py` repeats them) |
| `graph/src/neonradar_graph/migrate.py` | `APPLIED`, `RECORD`, `AWAIT_INDEXES` | Applied migrations, the `:SchemaMigration` record, waiting for indexes |
| `graph/src/neonradar_graph/onboarding.py` | `LOAD_NODES`, `LOAD_PARENTS`, `COUNT_NODES`, `RESET` | Assignment 1 (`neonradar onboarding check` also runs the queries in `docs/team/first-queries.md`) |
| `graph/src/neonradar_graph/loader.py` | `APPLIED`, `WIPE`, `STATS`, `node_query()` | Pending-migration check, `graph wipe`, `apoc.meta.stats`, node upserts built per schema (M2.11 moved the relationship upserts into `graph/src/neonradar_graph/queries/`) |
| `graph/tests/test_invariants.py` | I1 to I6 | Test strings; M2.11 wrote the same checks as counts into `graph/src/neonradar_graph/queries/verify_base.cypher` |
| `detect/src/neonradar_detect/runner.py` | `MERGE_RUN`, `PRUNE_RUN`, `MERGE_ALERTS` | Detection runs and alerts |
| `api/src/neonradar_api/entities.py`, `alerts.py`, `reference.py` (M1.9c, #44) | `FULLTEXT`, `ACCOUNT`, `ROOT`, `_HOP`, `_END`; `QUEUE`, `PAYLOAD`, `EVIDENCE`; `RECORD_COUNTS` | Search, entity detail and network, the alert queue and alert evidence, the meta counts; M2.12 moves the ones it changes into `.cypher` files |

The `.cypher` files on `main` are `graph/schema/migrations/0001_init.cypher` and the circular-flow template; `make cypher-lint` checks 32 statements (29 plus the template's three lint variants) with 0 problems. The API queries of M1.9c (#44) merged as Python strings (above); a later milestone that changes one moves it into a `.cypher` file that passes the lint.
